function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Best City to Visit for Ice‑Hockey Fans in Iceland** | Rank | City | Why It’s Ideal | |------|------|----------------| | **1** | **Reykjavík** | • Home to *Skát*’s flagship arena—often referred to simply as “the Ice Hall” —which hosts the entire Icelandic Premier League season, playoffs, and occasional international fixtures.
• Public skating hours, beginner clinics, and junior leagues run out of the same complex, so you can experience the sport from multiple angles.
• Central location makes it easy to hop between games, sightseeing spots (Harpa Concert Hall, Sun Voyager sculpture, Old Harbour), and world‑class dining options.
• Excellent transport links (airport shuttle, buses, taxis) and plenty of accommodation choices ranging from boutique guesthouses to luxury hotels. | --- ### Quick Highlights of Reykjavík’s Ice‑Hockey Scene | Feature | Details | |---------|--------| | **Main Arena** | *“Skítuhallinn”* (literally “The Skate Hall”) – built in 2018, seating around 600 spectators, equipped with modern lighting and sound systems. Hosts domestic league matches, playoff finals, and occasionally European club friendlies. | | **Local Club** | *Skautafélag Reykjavíkur (SRK)* – one of Iceland’s oldest and most successful teams, playing their home games here. Their fan base is passionate yet welcoming to newcomers. | | **Youth & Community Programs** | Daily skate rentals, free introductory hockey classes for kids aged 7–12, and weekend pick‑up games for adults. Many volunteers welcome tourists who wish to try a short lesson or two. | | **Events Calendar** | Check the *Úrvalsdeild Karla* schedule online; the regular season runs May through September, while the winter months feature exhibition tours and charity matches. | | **Accessibility** | Located just minutes from Keflavík International Airport (via direct bus line 55). Within walking distance of the city center, making it convenient whether you’re staying in a hostel or a five‑star hotel. | --- #### Alternative Option: Akureyri If you’d rather avoid crowds and enjoy a more intimate setting, Akureyri’s *“Akureyraklukkan”* rink serves as the hub for the town’s single professional team (*Þór Akureyri*) and several youth squads. While the venue is smaller (~300 seats), the community feel is strong, and you’ll often get chances to chat directly with coaches and players after games. --- ### Practical Tips for Visiting 1. **Book Tickets Early:** Game days fill up fast, especially when the national team visits or during the summer tournament series. 2. **Combine With Other Attractions:** Pair your match day with a whale‑watch cruise, a dip in the Blue Lagoon, or a hike along the Reykjadalur hot springs trail—all within a few hours' drive. 3. **Check Weather Forecast:** Even though the arena is indoors, outdoor activities nearby may require appropriate gear. Enjoy the thrill of watching Iceland’s rising talent play under bright lights, then unwind exploring the vibrant culture and natural wonders that make this Nordic capital truly unforgettable!
